intro.title: Default Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays a user's name and age, using TypeScript to define its props. You will learn how to set default values for props, so the component shows a friendly fallback message if certain information is not provided. The core concept is using default parameters in a function component to ensure your UI remains predictable and user-friendly. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces to define prop types and the ES6 default parameter syntax to assign these defaults. By the end, you'll have a reusable component that gracefully handles missing data.
intro.usecase: Default props are essential for creating reusable UI components that maintain consistent behavior across different contexts. In real applications, you'll see this pattern in design system components like buttons, input fields, and modals that need sensible fallback values when not fully configured. For example, a dashboard card component might have default padding and border radius, or a form input might have a default placeholder text when none is specified. This pattern prevents UI inconsistencies and reduces repetitive prop passing, making components more robust and easier to maintain in large-scale applications.
